Eight places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes in a
real Lakeshore document. All were checked and loading at the time this page was written.

- **[FDA guidance page: Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's Facility](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)**
  — FDA's own guidance-database listing for the document this lesson quotes throughout (final,
  April 2013, CBER). Use this page to confirm you're citing the current, final version, and to
  download the PDF directly from FDA rather than a mirror.

- **[21 CFR 211.68, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.68)**
  — the regulation behind "validation before routine use" and the record-retention citation this
  lesson names (211.68(b)). Cornell's free, citable, plain-text CFR mirror — use it when you need
  to hand someone the regulation itself without an eCFR login or PDF.

- **[21 CFR 606.160, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)**
  — the quality-control-records section (606.160(b)(5)(ii)) that FDA's BECS guidance cites
  alongside 211.68(b) and 211.100(b) for retaining validation records. Read it when you need the
  retention requirement's own regulatory text, not just the guidance's citation of it.

- **[FDA guidance page: General Principles of Software Validation](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-principles-software-validation)**
  — the January 2002 guidance FDA's BECS guidance itself points to (as "Ref. 1") for concepts
  like "level of confidence" and software regression testing. Written for device manufacturers,
  not user facilities like Lakeshore, but useful background on where the BECS guidance's own
  vocabulary comes from.

- **[IQ OQ PQ Explained for Computerised Systems and Equipment | Matrix Validate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7keFOP71UIw)**
  (Matrix One, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. An industry
  training explainer of the three qualification stages; not FDA-, BECS-, or blood-specific, so
  use it for vocabulary only. This page found no video that is specifically about traceability
  matrices and independently verifiable. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, Second Edition](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the publisher's page for the industry-practice guide behind the IQ/OQ/PQ vocabulary. Read
  it to see what the guide is and who it is for, and to remember it is industry practice, not
  regulation (the guide itself is sold, not free). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR 211.100, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.100)**
  — written procedures and deviations; the third regulation FDA's BECS guidance cites for
  retaining validation records (211.100(b)). Read it for the regulation's own text on
  documenting deviations from procedures. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA guidance page: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures: Scope and Application](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/part-11-electronic-records-electronic-signatures-scope-and-application)**
  — FDA's 2003 guidance on how it approaches Part 11, including validation. Not needed for this
  module, but it is the document module 5 uses to explain why validation is enforced through
  predicate rules; read it ahead if a matrix row references a Part 11 control. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about qualification protocols and requirements traceability.

- **[A Basic Guide to IQ, OQ, PQ in FDA-Regulated Industries](https://www.thefdagroup.com/blog/a-basic-guide-to-iq-oq-pq-in-fda-regulated-industries)** (The FDA Group, consultancy blog) — a plain-language walk through the three qualification stages. Useful as a second explanation of what each stage proves. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[IQ, OQ, PQ: what's needed for equipment validation in life sciences?](https://www.cognidox.com/blog/iq-oq-pq-equipment-validation)** (Cognidox, vendor blog) — covers the stages and the evidence each one produces. Vendor content, so use it for orientation, not as authority. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Requirements Traceability Matrix (Trace Matrix, RTM, TM)](https://www.ofnisystems.com/services/validation/traceability-matrix/)** (Ofni Systems, validation-software vendor) — a short explainer on linking requirements to tests, with examples of forward and backward tracing. Helps when you build or review a matrix row. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Understanding the Basics: What is a Traceability Matrix?](https://community.atlassian.com/forums/App-Central-articles/Understanding-the-Basics-What-is-a-Traceability-Matrix/ba-p/3284149)** (Atlassian Community, vendor article) — a general (not life-science-specific) primer on traceability matrices and gap-finding. Good for the concept; map the vocabulary to the lesson yourself. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
